div.head: I Cn 20.1
div.ab: Forðam eall þæt we æfre for rihthlafordhelde doð, eall we hit doð us sylfum to mycelre þearfe; forþam [þam] byð witodlice God hold, þe byð his hlaforde rihtlice hold.
Forþam eall þæt we afre for rihthlafordhelde doð, eall we hit doð us silfum to mycelre ðearfe; forþam þam bið God hold, þe bið his hlaforde hold.
Forðam eall þæt we æfre for rihthlafordhylde doð, eall we doð hit us sylfum to mycelre ðéarfe; forðam ðam bið witodlice God hold, ðe biþ his hlaforde rihtlice hold.
quia quicquid pro recta dominorum fidelitate facimus, ad magnam nobis utilitatem facimus; et scienter Deus illi fidelis est, qui domino suo recte fidelis est.
Forðam eall þæt we æfre for rihthlafordhylde doð, eall we doð hit us sylfum to mycelre ðéarfe, forðam ðam bið witodlice God hold ðe biþ his hlaforde rihtlice hold.
For all that we ever do, through just fidelity to our lord, we do to our own great advantage, for truly God shall be gracious to him who is justly faithful to his lord.
Denn alles was wir je aus echter Treue gegen den Herrn thun, das alles thun wir uns selbst zu grossem Nutzen; denn gewisslich dem wird Gott gnädig sein, der seinem Herrn recht getreu ist.
For all that we ever do out of true loyalty to our lord, we do it all to our own great benefit; for God will certainly be gracious to him who is rightly loyal to his lord.
div.note: ‘þam’ supplied in G from the other MSS and Wulfstan homilies (119, 299).; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
